title: Common Cold
whenToSeeDoctor: If symptoms last more than 10 days, fever stays above 38.5°C for more than three days, breathing becomes difficult, symptoms improve and then worsen, or chest pain develops.
homeCare: Rest, plenty of fluids, paracetamol for pain or fever, saline nose drops or steam for congestion. Antibiotics do not treat a cold — it is viral.

source.authority: WHO / SA NDoH Standard Treatment Guidelines (PHC)

title: Influenza (Flu)
whenToSeeDoctor: If there is shortness of breath, chest pain, confusion, fever beyond three days, or if the person is pregnant, over 65, living with HIV, or has a chronic condition such as diabetes, heart disease or asthma.
homeCare: Rest at home, fluids, paracetamol for fever and aches. Yearly flu vaccination before winter is recommended for pregnant women, older people and those with chronic illness.

title: COVID-19
whenToSeeDoctor: Seek urgent care for struggling to breathe, chest pain, confusion, bluish lips or face, or inability to keep fluids down. People with diabetes, HIV, heart or lung disease are at higher risk of severe illness.
homeCare: Most people recover at home: rest, fluids, paracetamol for fever, and staying away from others while infectious. Vaccination reduces severe disease.

title: Sinusitis
whenToSeeDoctor: If symptoms last more than 10 days, worsen after improving, fever is above 39°C, or there is swelling around the eye — swelling around the eye needs urgent care.
homeCare: Steam inhalation, saline rinses, fluids, paracetamol or ibuprofen for pain. Most cases are viral and settle without antibiotics.

title: Acute Bronchitis
symptoms: cough lasting one to three weeks
whenToSeeDoctor: If the cough lasts more than three weeks (TB must be excluded in South Africa), there is blood in the sputum, breathlessness, or fever that will not settle.
homeCare: Rest, fluids, warm drinks, paracetamol. Antibiotics are usually not needed — most cases are viral. Avoid smoke.

source.authority: SA NDoH Standard Treatment Guidelines (PHC) / WHO

title: Pneumonia
symptoms: tiredness and confusion in older people
whenToSeeDoctor: Pneumonia always needs a clinical assessment — go to the clinic the same day. Call 10177 for an ambulance if there is severe breathlessness, blue lips, confusion, or the person cannot keep fluids down.
homeCare: Pneumonia is treated with antibiotics prescribed by a clinician. Finish the full course even when feeling better. Rest, fluids and paracetamol support recovery.

source.authority: SA NDoH Standard Treatment Guidelines (PHC) / WHO

title: Asthma
symptoms: cough at night or early morning
whenToSeeDoctor: If a reliever inhaler is needed more than twice a week, night-time waking with symptoms occurs, or symptoms limit activity — the preventer treatment may need review. Call 10177 if the reliever is not helping, speech becomes difficult in full sentences, or lips turn blue.
homeCare: Use the preventer inhaler every day even when well, keep the reliever close, avoid smoke and known triggers, and follow the written action plan from the clinic.

title: Hypertension (High Blood Pressure)
whenToSeeDoctor: Every adult should have a blood pressure check at least every two years, and yearly after 40. Urgent care is needed for a reading above 180/120 with severe headache, chest pain, vision changes or weakness on one side.
homeCare: Cut salt to less than a teaspoon a day, keep to a healthy weight, exercise, limit alcohol, do not smoke, and take prescribed pills every day — blood pressure medicine works only while it is taken.

title: Angina (Heart-Related Chest Pain)
symptoms: chest pressure or tightness on exertion
pain spreading to arm, jaw or back
whenToSeeDoctor: Any new chest pain like this needs a clinic assessment soon. Call 10177 immediately if pain lasts more than 15 minutes at rest, comes with sweating, nausea or breathlessness — this may be a heart attack.
homeCare: Stop the activity and rest when pain comes. Take prescribed medicine as directed. Do not smoke — smoking narrows the heart arteries further.

source.authority: WHO / SA NDoH cardiovascular care guidelines

title: Heart Failure
whenToSeeDoctor: Same-week clinic visit for new or worsening swelling and breathlessness. Urgent care for sudden severe breathlessness, coughing pink frothy sputum, or chest pain.
homeCare: Take water tablets as prescribed, weigh daily (report a gain of more than 2 kg in three days), limit salt, keep active within ability, and never stop heart medicine without a clinician.

source.authority: SA NDoH / WHO heart failure guidance

title: Stroke
whenToSeeDoctor: This is an emergency. Call 10177 at the first sign — treatment within the first hours can prevent lasting damage. Note the exact time symptoms started and say so to the ambulance crew.
homeCare: While waiting: keep the person calm and seated or lying safely, give nothing to eat or drink, and stay with them.

source.authority: WHO / SA NDoH stroke care guidance

title: Deep Vein Thrombosis (Blood Clot in Leg)
whenToSeeDoctor: See a doctor the same day for a swollen, painful leg. Call 10177 if breathlessness or chest pain follows — a clot may have moved to the lungs.
homeCare: Do not massage the leg. Treatment is blood-thinning medicine prescribed after assessment. On long journeys, stand and walk every two hours.

title: Gastroenteritis (Stomach Bug)
whenToSeeDoctor: Same-day care for infants, older people, blood in the stool, signs of dehydration (sunken eyes, dry mouth, passing little urine, drowsiness), or vomiting everything for more than a day. Diarrhoea lasting more than a few days needs assessment.
homeCare: Sip oral rehydration solution continuously — a sachet from the pharmacy mixed in clean water. Children get zinc for 10-14 days. Keep eating small light meals. Hand washing stops it spreading.

title: Constipation
symptoms: passing stools fewer than three times a week
whenToSeeDoctor: If there is blood in the stool, a sudden change in bowel habit after age 45, weight loss, constant tummy pain, or no improvement after two weeks of home care.
homeCare: Drink more water, add fibre gradually (fruit, vegetables, whole grains, beans), walk daily, respond to the urge to go, and set a regular toilet time.

title: Haemorrhoids (Piles)
symptoms: bright red blood on the paper
whenToSeeDoctor: If bleeding keeps recurring, is dark or mixed into the stool, or comes with a change in bowel habit — these need examination to rule out bowel disease.
homeCare: More fibre and water, warm sits baths for comfort, avoid straining and long phone-sitting on the toilet, and paracetamol for pain.

title: Heartburn and Reflux (GERD)
symptoms: burning pain behind the breastbone after meals
whenToSeeDoctor: If symptoms continue beyond two weeks despite home care, swallowing becomes difficult or painful, there is weight loss, or vomiting blood — vomiting blood or black stools are urgent.
homeCare: Smaller meals, nothing for three hours before bed, raise the head of the bed, cut down spicy and fatty foods, coffee, alcohol and smoking. A short course of a pharmacy antacid or acid-blocker can help.

title: Peptic Ulcer
symptoms: burning pain in the upper tummy
pain eased or worsened by food
whenToSeeDoctor: Black tarry stools, vomiting blood or coffee-ground material, or sudden severe tummy pain need emergency care. Ongoing tummy pain deserves a clinic visit — ulcers are often caused by H. pylori bacteria, which is treatable.
homeCare: Avoid ibuprofen and similar anti-inflammatory tablets unless a clinician prescribes them, limit alcohol, stop smoking, eat regular meals. Acid-blocking medicine helps while the cause is treated.

title: Intestinal Worms
symptoms: itching around the anus at night (threadworms)
poor appetite or slow weight gain in children
whenToSeeDoctor: If a child loses weight, the tummy swells, or symptoms continue after treatment. In South Africa, children are dewormed routinely at clinics and schools.
homeCare: Deworming medicine (mebendazole) treats most worms — treat the whole household for threadworms, wash hands and nails, wash bedding, and wash fruit and vegetables.

source.authority: WHO / SA NDoH EPI deworming programme

title: Low Back Pain
whenToSeeDoctor: Urgent care for loss of bladder or bowel control, numbness between the legs, or leg weakness. Clinic visit for back pain with fever, unexplained weight loss, night pain, after a fall, or if pain has not improved in six weeks.
homeCare: Keep moving — bed rest slows recovery. Warmth, gentle stretching, paracetamol or ibuprofen, and a firm mattress help most people within four to six weeks.

title: Ankle Sprain
whenToSeeDoctor: If the ankle cannot take any weight, looks deformed, the skin is broken, or there is numbness. Also if there is no improvement after a week of proper care.
homeCare: Rest the ankle, ice wrapped in a cloth 15-20 minutes at a time, a firm bandage, and keep the foot raised for the first two to three days. Gentle movement and balancing exercises as pain allows.

title: Osteoarthritis
symptoms: morning stiffness under half an hour
knee, hip or hand joints most often
whenToSeeDoctor: When pain limits walking, work or sleep — a clinician can confirm the cause, arrange physiotherapy and adjust medicine. Sudden hot, swollen single joints need same-day assessment (possible gout or infection).
homeCare: Keep moving within comfort — strong muscles protect joints. Weight loss takes real load off knees and hips. Paracetamol first, warm packs for stiffness.

title: Gout
symptoms: sudden severe pain in the big toe or another joint
extreme tenderness — even a sheet hurts
whenToSeeDoctor: Same-day care for a first attack or a severe one — treatment works best early. Repeated attacks need long-term medicine to protect joints and kidneys.
homeCare: Rest and raise the joint, ice wrapped in a cloth, plenty of water. Cut back beer, sugary drinks, organ meats and large meat portions.

title: Tendinitis (Tennis Elbow, Shoulder Tendinitis)
symptoms: pain at a specific tendon with movement
tenderness over the outer elbow or shoulder
whenToSeeDoctor: If pain persists beyond two to three weeks, the joint cannot be moved, or there was a sudden pop with weakness — that can be a tear.
homeCare: Reduce the repetitive activity (not total rest), ice after activity, paracetamol or ibuprofen short-term, and gentle stretching once pain settles.

title: Migraine
symptoms: throbbing headache often on one side
sometimes visual aura before the headache
whenToSeeDoctor: Emergency care for a sudden worst-ever headache, headache with fever and stiff neck, confusion, weakness or a first severe headache after age 50. Clinic visit if attacks are frequent (more than four a month) or disrupt work.
homeCare: Rest in a dark quiet room early in the attack, simple painkillers taken at the first sign work best, regular sleep and meals, and note personal triggers (missed meals, stress, certain foods).

title: Tension Headache
whenToSeeDoctor: If headaches occur more than 10 days a month (overuse of painkillers can worsen them), or any red-flag pattern appears — sudden onset, fever, weakness, or waking from sleep with pain.
homeCare: Regular sleep, water, screen breaks, neck stretches, stress management, and limited painkillers — painkillers on more than 10 days a month can cause rebound headaches.

title: Epilepsy
whenToSeeDoctor: Call 10177 for any seizure lasting more than five minutes, seizures repeating without recovery, a first-ever seizure, injury, or a seizure in water. Routine clinic care keeps medicine doses right.
homeCare: Take anti-seizure medicine daily without gaps — stopping suddenly causes seizures. Keep regular sleep, limit alcohol, avoid swimming alone and heights, and tell close contacts what to do during a seizure.

title: Peripheral Neuropathy (Nerve Pain in Feet)
symptoms: burning or pins-and-needles in the feet
whenToSeeDoctor: Any new numbness or burning feet needs assessment — diabetes, HIV and TB medicines are common causes. Urgent care for a foot wound that is not felt or not healing.
homeCare: Check feet daily by looking (use a mirror for soles), wash and dry between toes, wear closed shoes that fit, never walk barefoot, and keep the underlying condition controlled.

title: Eczema (Atopic Dermatitis)
symptoms: commonly in elbow and knee creases
whenToSeeDoctor: If the skin weeps, crusts or has pus (possible infection), flares are frequent, or sleep is broken by itch. Babies and children with widespread eczema need a clinic plan.
homeCare: Moisturise generously and often, avoid harsh soap and very hot water, keep nails short, use a prescribed steroid cream short-term on flares, and known triggers (detergents, certain fabrics).

title: Acne
symptoms: deeper painful lumps on face, chest or back
most often teenagers and young adults
whenToSeeDoctor: If acne is deep, scarring, painful or affecting confidence — effective prescription treatments exist. Sudden severe acne with other symptoms in women may point to a hormone cause.
homeCare: Wash gently twice daily, do not squeeze or pick, use non-greasy products, give treatments six to eight weeks to work.

title: Ringworm (Fungal Skin Infection)
symptoms: ring-shaped scaly patch with a clear centre
can affect scalp, body, feet (athlete's foot) or groin
whenToSeeDoctor: If the scalp is involved (needs tablets, not cream), there is no improvement after two weeks of cream, or the person has diabetes or a weakened immune system.
homeCare: Antifungal cream twice daily, continuing a week beyond the rash clearing. Dry skin folds properly, do not share towels or clothes, and wash bedding hot.

title: Scabies
symptoms: thin burrow lines between fingers, on wrists, waist
itching in close contacts at the same time
whenToSeeDoctor: For treatment cream — everyone in the house must be treated on the same day, so a clinic plan helps. Infants, pregnant women and crusted widespread rash need clinician care.
homeCare: Apply permethrin cream as directed to the whole body, wash clothes and bedding on the hottest cycle that day, and trim nails. Itch can continue one to two weeks after successful treatment.

title: Impetigo (School Sores)
symptoms: honey-coloured crusts around nose and mouth
whenToSeeDoctor: If sores spread despite hygiene, there are many lesions, or the child is unwell with fever — antibiotics may be needed.
homeCare: Gently wash crusts away with clean water and soap, keep nails short, do not share towels, and keep children home until sores stop weeping or treatment has started.

title: Chickenpox
symptoms: blisters crust over in about a week
whenToSeeDoctor: If blisters become infected (redness, pus), the person is pregnant, a newborn is affected, or there is drowsiness, repeated vomiting or breathing difficulty. Keep away from pregnant women who have not had chickenpox.
homeCare: Cool baths, calamine lotion, paracetamol for fever (never aspirin or ibuprofen for chickenpox in children), short nails, loose clothes. Contagious until every blister has crusted.

title: Shingles (Herpes Zoster)
symptoms: burning pain in a band on one side of the body
clusters of blisters on red skin
whenToSeeDoctor: See a doctor as soon as the rash starts — antiviral tablets work best within 72 hours. Same-day care if the rash is near the eye, there is weakness, or the immune system is weakened (for example by HIV).
homeCare: Keep the rash clean and dry, loose clothing, paracetamol for pain. Shingles is contagious to people who have never had chickenpox until blisters scab.

title: Type 2 Diabetes
whenToSeeDoctor: Ask for a glucose test with any of these symptoms, or with risk factors — family history, overweight, age over 45, high blood pressure. Urgent care for drowsiness, rapid breathing, fruity-smelling breath, or a wound that will not heal.
homeCare: Once diagnosed: daily medicine without gaps, regular meals with less sugar and refined starch, walking most days, daily foot checks, and clinic reviews for eyes, feet and kidneys.

title: Hypothyroidism (Underactive Thyroid)
whenToSeeDoctor: A blood test at the clinic confirms it. Review is needed if symptoms return while on treatment, or if new fast or irregular heartbeat, sweating and weight loss appear (overactive).
homeCare: Take levothyroxine on an empty stomach with water, 30-60 minutes before food, at the same time daily, and keep clinic blood tests — the dose is adjusted from them.

source.authority: SA NDoH Standard Treatment Guidelines / WHO

title: Hyperthyroidism (Overactive Thyroid)
whenToSeeDoctor: See a doctor for these symptoms — treatment protects the heart and bones. Urgent care for fever with severe symptoms, agitation or confusion (thyroid storm).
homeCare: Follow clinic monitoring closely, stop smoking (smoking worsens thyroid eye disease), and limit caffeine while symptoms are active.

source.authority: SA NDoH Standard Treatment Guidelines / WHO

title: Tuberculosis (TB)
symptoms: cough for more than two weeks
whenToSeeDoctor: Anyone with a cough longer than two weeks should give sputum at a clinic — testing and treatment are free. Coughing blood or severe breathlessness needs urgent care. Close contacts and people living with HIV should be screened.
homeCare: Treatment takes six months and must be finished even when feeling well — stopping early breeds drug resistance. Take tablets as directed, eat well, keep the room ventilated, and cover coughs.

title: HIV Infection
symptoms: two to four weeks after infection: fever, rash, sore throat, swollen glands, flu-like illness
whenToSeeDoctor: The only way to know is a test — free at any clinic, or an HIV self-test kit. Treatment (ART) is free and started immediately. After any possible exposure, post-exposure prophylaxis works best within 72 hours — go to a clinic urgently.
homeCare: Once on treatment, one tablet a day keeps the virus suppressed — take it at the same time daily, never skip, and keep viral load appointments. On effective treatment a person cannot pass HIV through sex.

source.authority: SA NDoH HIV guidelines (test and treat) / WHO

title: Measles
symptoms: rash starting behind the ears and hairline then spreading down
small white spots inside the cheeks
whenToSeeDoctor: Measles needs a clinic assessment — complications include pneumonia, diarrhoea and brain inflammation. Urgent care for drowsiness, convulsions, fast breathing or dehydration.
homeCare: Rest, fluids, paracetamol, vitamin A as given by the clinic, and keep the child away from others until at least four days after the rash appears. Immunisation (at 6 and 12 months in the SA schedule) prevents it.

title: Malaria
symptoms: can occur weeks after a visit to a malaria area
whenToSeeDoctor: Any fever within weeks — even months — after visiting a malaria area (north-eastern Limpopo, the Lowveld of Mpumalanga including Kruger Park, northern KwaZulu-Natal) needs a same-day malaria test. Emergency care for confusion, yellow eyes, dark urine or bleeding.
homeCare: Prevention: take prophylaxis as prescribed, sleep under a treated net, use repellent, and cover arms and legs at dusk and dawn. There is no effective home treatment — malaria is treated with prescribed tablets.

title: Hepatitis B
symptoms: acute: tiredness, yellow eyes, dark urine, tummy pain, loss of appetite
whenToSeeDoctor: Testing is recommended in pregnancy, before immunisation decisions, and for household or sexual contacts of a person with hepatitis B. Chronic infection needs lifelong monitoring for liver damage. Yellow eyes or severe vomiting need urgent care.
homeCare: Avoid alcohol (it accelerates liver damage), tell close contacts to test and vaccinate, never share razors or toothbrushes, and use condoms. The childhood vaccine protects the next generation.

title: Meningitis
symptoms: rash that does not fade when pressed
in babies: bulging fontanelle, high-pitched cry, drowsiness, poor feeding
whenToSeeDoctor: This is an emergency — call 10177 or go straight to a hospital. Minutes matter, especially with the non-fading rash.
homeCare: None — this is not treatable at home. While waiting for help, keep the person still, dim lights, and give nothing by mouth.

title: Depression
symptoms: low mood most of the day
loss of enjoyment in things once enjoyed
whenToSeeDoctor: If symptoms last more than two weeks, work or relationships suffer, or there are any thoughts of self-harm — help is available immediately (SADAG 0800 567 567, Lifeline 0861 322 322).
homeCare: Keep a daily routine, gentle exercise, stay connected to people, limit alcohol, and break tasks into small steps. Depression is treatable — counselling and medicine both work.

source.authority: WHO / SA NDoH mental health guidelines; SADAG

title: Anxiety
symptoms: worry that is hard to control
whenToSeeDoctor: If worry or panic stops work, study or relationships, panic attacks keep happening, or alcohol is being used to cope.
homeCare: Slow breathing (longer out-breath than in-breath), regular exercise, less caffeine and nicotine, good sleep habits, and talking to someone trusted. Panic attacks are frightening but not dangerous.

source.authority: WHO / SA NDoH mental health guidelines; SADAG

title: Urinary Tract Infection (UTI)
whenToSeeDoctor: Same-day care — UTIs usually need prescribed antibiotics. Urgent care for fever, flank (loin) pain, or vomiting — the infection may have reached the kidneys. Men, pregnant women, children and catheter users always need assessment.
homeCare: Drink extra water, paracetamol for pain, and finish the full antibiotic course. Passing urine after sex and wiping from front to back help prevent recurrences.

title: Kidney Stones
symptoms: severe waves of pain from the loin to the groin
restlessness — cannot find a comfortable position
whenToSeeDoctor: Go for urgent assessment — pain control and imaging are needed. Emergency care if there is fever with the pain, or inability to pass urine.
homeCare: Drink water steadily through the day once assessed. Small stones often pass with pain relief. Reducing salt and animal protein and drinking enough water lower recurrence.

title: Benign Prostatic Enlargement (BPH)
symptoms: waking at night to pass urine
whenToSeeDoctor: A clinic assessment confirms it and rules out prostate cancer (examination and a blood test). Urgent care for complete inability to pass urine, or blood in urine.
homeCare: Reduce evening fluids and caffeine, allow time to empty the bladder fully, and limit cold medicines containing decongestants — they worsen the blockage.

title: Conjunctivitis (Pink Eye)
symptoms: discharge that may stick lashes together
whenToSeeDoctor: Same-day care for eye pain, light sensitivity, blurred vision, or if a contact lens wearer — these suggest a more serious infection. Newborns with sticky or red eyes need urgent care. No improvement after three to four days also needs review.
homeCare: Bathe lids with clean water, wipe from inner to outer corner with a fresh cloth each time, do not share towels, avoid contact lenses and eye make-up, and wash hands often.

title: Stye (Eyelid Gland Infection)
symptoms: painful red lump on the eyelid margin
whenToSeeDoctor: If it does not settle within one to two weeks, keeps recurring, the whole lid or face swells, or vision is affected.
homeCare: Warm (not hot) compress held on the lid for 10 minutes, three to four times a day, gently massaging the lid. Do not squeeze or poke it, and avoid eye make-up until healed.

title: Period Pain (Dysmenorrhoea)
symptoms: cramping lower tummy pain in the first one to two days of a period
whenToSeeDoctor: If pain worsens over months, occurs between periods, comes with heavy bleeding or pain during sex — endometriosis, fibroids or infection need to be ruled out. Pain that stops school or work every month deserves care.
homeCare: Heat pack on the lower tummy, early and regular ibuprofen or paracetamol at the first twinge, gentle exercise, and enough sleep.

title: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID)
whenToSeeDoctor: See a doctor promptly — PID needs antibiotic courses, and untreated it causes infertility and ectopic pregnancy. Emergency care for severe pain, vomiting or fainting. Partners need treatment too.
homeCare: Complete the full antibiotic course, rest, paracetamol, and no sex until both partners finish treatment. Condoms prevent the infections that cause it.

title: Vaginal Thrush (Candidiasis)
symptoms: stinging during sex or when passing urine
whenToSeeDoctor: If this is the first episode, it recurs four or more times a year, there is diabetes or pregnancy, or the discharge smells, is greenish or comes with bleeding — an STI check is then wise.
homeCare: Antifungal cream or pessaries from the pharmacy treat most episodes, and treating a precipitating factor (recent antibiotics, uncontrolled sugar, tight synthetic underwear) prevents repeat.

title: Menopause
whenToSeeDoctor: Any bleeding after a year without periods needs prompt assessment. Severe symptoms or early menopause (before 40) deserve a clinic conversation about bone and heart health and treatment options.
homeCare: Weight-bearing exercise, enough calcium, dress in layers, cut caffeine and alcohol, and sleep hygiene. Symptoms ease over years for most women.

title: Uterine Fibroids
whenToSeeDoctor: For very heavy bleeding (soaking a pad an hour, clots, tiredness from anaemia), rapidly growing swelling, severe pain, or difficulty falling pregnant. Heavy bleeding over months causes anaemia — check it.
homeCare: Iron-rich food with the anaemia that heavy periods cause, and heat for cramps. Most fibroids are benign; size and symptoms decide treatment, which ranges from tablets to procedures.

title: Croup
symptoms: child usually between six months and three years
whenToSeeDoctor: Urgent care for stridor at rest, drooling or struggling to swallow, blue lips, or severe sucking-in of the chest wall. Croup that is mild may still need a clinic check.
homeCare: Keep the child calm — crying worsens it. Cool night air or steamy bathroom air can ease a mild attack. Give paracetamol for fever and fluids in small sips.

title: Infant Colic
symptoms: crying more than three hours a day, more than three days a week
worse in the late afternoon and evening
whenToSeeDoctor: To rule out other causes when crying is severe — the same day if there is fever, poor feeding, repeated vomiting, blood in the nappy, or the baby is not gaining weight.
homeCare: Rhythmic soothing: gentle rocking, carrying, sucking (breast or dummy), white noise, and winding after feeds. It resolves by three to four months. Caring for a colicky baby is exhausting — parents need support and safe coping, never shaking.

title: Teething
whenToSeeDoctor: If fever stays above 38.5°C, there is diarrhoea or vomiting, or the baby refuses all feeds — teething does not cause high fever or illness, and something else may be wrong.
homeCare: A chilled (not frozen) teething ring, clean finger massage of the gums, and paracetamol at correct weight dose if very uncomfortable. Teething gels and necklaces are not recommended.

source.authority: SA NDoH (PHC) child guidance / SA Paediatric Association

title: Nappy Rash
symptoms: red skin in the nappy area
sometimes satellite spots at the edges (thrush)
whenToSeeDoctor: If there are blisters or pus, the rash does not improve after three to four days of care, or it spreads beyond the nappy area.
homeCare: Change nappies often, wash with water and pat dry, give nappy-free air time, and apply a zinc-oxide barrier cream each change. Angular red spots that spread suggest thrush, which needs an antifungal cream.

title: Febrile Convulsion
symptoms: a fit with fever in a child aged six months to five years
whenToSeeDoctor: Call 10177 if the seizure lasts more than five minutes, jerks one side only, the child turns blue, or does not wake properly afterwards. Any first seizure should be seen by a doctor the same day to find the fever's cause.
homeCare: During a fit: lay the child on their side on a soft surface, do not hold them down, put nothing in the mouth, and time it. Afterwards remove excess clothing and give paracetamol once awake. Most children outgrow them without lasting harm.

title: Otitis Media (Middle Ear Infection)
symptoms: irritability and pulling at the ear in small children
sometimes discharge if the drum bursts
whenToSeeDoctor: Children under two, both ears affected, discharge from the ear, severe pain, fever beyond two days, or swelling behind the ear (urgent). Many cases settle in 48 hours with pain relief alone.
homeCare: Paracetamol or ibuprofen at weight-correct doses, warm face cloth over the ear, and keep the ear dry if discharging. Never poke cotton buds into the ear.

title: Tonsillitis
symptoms: swollen tender glands in the neck
sometimes headache and tummy pain in children
whenToSeeDoctor: If the person cannot swallow fluids or is drooling (urgent — go now), breathing is noisy, or fever and pain are severe with no cough (may be strep throat needing penicillin). Frequent recurrent attacks need review.
homeCare: Cool drinks and soft food, warm salt-water gargles, paracetamol or ibuprofen. Most sore throats are viral and improve within a week.

title: Nosebleed (Epistaxis)
symptoms: bleeding from one or both nostrils
often after nose-picking, dry air, or a knock
whenToSeeDoctor: If bleeding does not stop after 20-30 minutes of firm pressure, is heavy after a head injury or fall (emergency), or nosebleeds keep recurring (blood pressure and other checks needed).
homeCare: Sit leaning forward, pinch the soft part of the nose firmly for 10 minutes without letting go, breathe through the mouth, and a cold cloth on the bridge helps. Do not tilt the head back — blood runs into the throat.

title: Diarrhoea in Children Under Five
whenToSeeDoctor: Immediately for any dehydration sign (sunken eyes, no urine for six hours, drowsiness, repeated vomiting), blood in the stool, or fever above 38.5°C. Diarrhoea lasting more than a week needs review.
homeCare: Oral rehydration solution after every loose stool, zinc for 10-14 days, keep breastfeeding and feeding — never starve a child with diarrhoea. Keep vaccines (rotavirus) up to date and hands washed.

source.authority: WHO / SA NDoH integrated management of childhood illness (IMCI)

title: Contact Dermatitis
symptoms: itchy skin where something touched it
red on lighter skin; dark brown, purple or grey on darker skin
often on the hands or face
appears within hours or days of the contact
whenToSeeDoctor: If it keeps coming back, is severe, does not settle with care at home, or you cannot work out what is causing it.
homeCare: Find and avoid what set it off — a soap, detergent, frequent wetting, nickel or a cosmetic. Use an unperfumed moisturiser (emollient) often and generously, wash with it instead of soap, and wear gloves for irritants.

source.authority: Written for MyThuso in its own words from the NHS website — Contact dermatitis (https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/contact-dermatitis/, reviewed 3 May 2023); checked against MedlinePlus — Rashes (https://medlineplus.gov/rashes.html) and CDC/NIOSH — Skin exposures (https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/skin-exposure/about/index.html)

title: Hives (Urticaria)
symptoms: pink or red on lighter skin, harder to see on darker skin
can appear anywhere and move around
each patch usually fades within a day or two
whenToSeeDoctor: If the rash lasts more than two days, spreads, keeps coming back, or comes with a fever or deep swelling, or you are worried about a child. Call 10177 (or 112 from a cellphone) at once if the lips, mouth, tongue or throat swell, breathing becomes hard, the lips turn blue or grey, or the person becomes confused or faints — that is a severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis).
homeCare: Most hives clear by themselves within a few days. Avoid hot baths and showers and tight clothing, and ask a pharmacist whether an over-the-counter antihistamine suits you, mentioning any long-term condition.

source.authority: Written for MyThuso in its own words from the NHS website — Hives (https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/hives/, reviewed 26 April 2024); checked against MedlinePlus — Hives (https://medlineplus.gov/hives.html) and Anaphylaxis (https://medlineplus.gov/anaphylaxis.html)

title: Cellulitis (Skin Infection)
symptoms: redness that spreads, which can be less obvious on darker skin
most often on the lower leg
whenToSeeDoctor: Be seen the same day if skin becomes painful, hot and swollen — early treatment stops it getting worse. Call 10177 (or 112 from a cellphone) if it comes with a high fever, a fast heartbeat, purple patches, dizziness, confusion, pale or clammy skin, or fainting.
homeCare: Cellulitis needs treatment from a clinician; care at home supports it and does not replace it. Raise the affected limb, gently move nearby joints, drink plenty, and afterwards keep the skin clean, moisturised and protected from cuts.

title: Sunburn
symptoms: redness, which may be less visible on darker skin
flaking or peeling a few days later
whenToSeeDoctor: If the skin is blistered or swollen, the person has a very high temperature, feels hot and shivery, or is very tired, dizzy, sick or has a headache or cramps — or if a baby or young child is sunburnt.
homeCare: Get out of the sun, cool the skin with a cool shower, bath or damp towels, then apply after-sun or an unperfumed moisturiser (emollient). Drink plenty of water and keep the burnt skin covered from the sun until it heals.

source.authority: Written for MyThuso in its own words from the NHS website — Sunburn (https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/sunburn/, reviewed 24 November 2025); checked against CDC — Heat-related illnesses (https://www.cdc.gov/disasters/extremeheat/pdf/Heat_Related_Illness.pdf)

title: Heat Rash (Prickly Heat)
symptoms: red on lighter skin; may look grey or white on darker skin
not catching, and common in babies
whenToSeeDoctor: If it has not improved after a few days, or you are worried about a baby's rash.
homeCare: Keep the skin cool so it stops sweating: loose cotton clothes, light bedding, cool baths or showers, plenty to drink, and a cold compress. Pat the skin rather than scratching, keep it dry, and avoid perfumed products and heavy creams.

source.authority: Written for MyThuso in its own words from the NHS website — Heat rash (https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/heat-rash-prickly-heat/, reviewed 9 May 2024); checked against CDC/NIOSH — Heat-related illnesses (https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/heat-stress/about/illnesses.html)

title: Insect Bites (Mosquito, Flea, Bedbug)
symptoms: flea bites often in groups below the knees
bedbug bites in lines or clusters on skin bared in bed
red or pink on lighter skin; brown or purple and harder to see on darker skin
children may get crops of very itchy bumps that keep coming back
whenToSeeDoctor: If a bite looks infected (hot, spreading redness, swelling or pus), stays very painful or swollen despite care at home, a baby under one year is bitten, or it gets worse or comes with a fever. Call 10177 (or 112 from a cellphone) if the face, lips or throat swell or breathing becomes difficult.
homeCare: Wash the area, hold a cool damp cloth on it to ease the itch and swelling, and keep nails short so scratching does not cause infection. Ask a pharmacist about an over-the-counter antihistamine if the itch spoils sleep.

source.authority: Written for MyThuso in its own words from the NHS website — Insect bites and stings (https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/insect-bites-and-stings/, reviewed 1 June 2023) and Bedbugs (https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/bedbugs/); checked against CDC — Mosquito bites (https://www.cdc.gov/mosquitoes/about/about-mosquito-bites.html) and Bed bugs (https://www.cdc.gov/bed-bugs/about/index.html)

title: Severe Skin Reaction to a Medicine (Stevens-Johnson Syndrome)
symptoms: a flu-like illness first: fever, sore throat, aching
then a fast-spreading rash of round patches, darker in the middle
painful sores in the mouth and throat
sore eyes that hurt in bright light
whenToSeeDoctor: This is an emergency. Call 10177 (or 112 from a cellphone) if a spreading rash blisters or peels, especially after starting a new medicine (in South Africa this includes some HIV and epilepsy medicines), or if there is trouble breathing, a tight chest or throat, or a swollen face or eyes.
homeCare: There is no care at home for this. Do not drive yourself: call an ambulance or have someone take you, and bring every medicine being taken, and any stopped in recent weeks.

source.authority: Written for MyThuso in its own words from the NHS website — Stevens-Johnson syndrome (https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/stevens-johnson-syndrome/, reviewed 4 March 2026); checked against MedlinePlus Genetics — Stevens-Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis (https://medlineplus.gov/genetics/condition/stevens-johnson-syndrome-toxic-epidermal-necrolysis/)
